out_of_sample.aggregation: one item per structure-kind truth register, except a synchronizer register of a declared chain unit, which is counted through its unit, plus one item per declared structure-kind unit; found = matched a harness-verified structure of an accepted kind at IoU > 0.5; exact = equal flop sets and verified; both libraries pooled (a design contributes twice). This is review[2]'s own aggregation, and the one every published holdout figure has used.
caveats: The corpus is SYNTHETIC and was written by the same project as the recognizer; several of its classes (cohort 2) were added because the generalisation regression set showed them missing (changes.jsonl C23, C31). It is the best out-of-sample estimate that survives this round, not an independent one.

The generalisation regression sets (out/s3/review_generalisation, review_generalisation2) are NO LONGER held out: counter.py, lfsr.py, shift.py, controls.py and verify.py all consulted them (changes.jsonl C25).

TEMPO is the development design: every TEMPO figure is in-sample. Four recognizer fixes were traced from TEMPO misses by truth name (changes.jsonl C27-C30), and PC03, PC06, PC07, PC09, C01-C06, C10 and C21(d) were selected on TEMPO.
These rates come from ONE seeded corpus evaluation; they carry no confidence interval.

They describe the recognizer AND the harness verifier as of source.code_sha256: 'found' means the harness verified the structure, so a change to tools/s3/verify.py moves them as surely as a change to a recognizer module (review[1] issue 2).

THE false_positive_structures COLUMN OVERSTATES; found / exact and their denominators do NOT. out/s3/review_generalisation2/evaluate.py's outcomes() builds its item list from truth registers whose kind is in STRUCTURE_KINDS, so a 'flag' register's alt_kinds are never consulted. Under the truth's TOGGLE_RULE a 1-bit toggle is kind 'flag' with alt_kinds ['counter'] -- the truth EXPLICITLY ACCEPTS a counter over it -- yet such a prediction matches no item there and is scored a false positive. Counted on the evaluation this document was derived from, as false-positive structures of width 1 lying entirely in one truth register of kind 'flag': holdout 2 of 6, train 10 of 16. The overstatement is in the CONSERVATIVE direction. tools/s3/score.py -- the scorer every published table comes from -- does not make this error: score.Truth builds accepts from alt_kinds for EVERY truth register, a flag included. The scoring rule is left as it is on purpose: changing it would move a published out-of-sample number without a lead decision (changes.jsonl T04, T14).

ledger.git_head_explanation: FREEZE.json.git_head is 75803221bc29, the commit that was HEAD when freeze write ran -- necessarily the PARENT of the freeze commit itself, since the commit cannot contain its own hash. The freeze commit is 232cfe67545a ('S3: freeze the first slice of structure recognition before the blind evaluation'), and every run record's top-level git_head is that commit: the runs executed on the frozen tree. Each record's freeze.git_head reproduces FREEZE.json's value. The two fields are different by construction and neither is a mismatch.
ledger.hash_semantics: record['attempt']['record_sha256'] hashes the ATTEMPT file (blind-<id>-<utc>-<hash>.attempt.json), not the final run record. The final record's own sha256 is carried by the ledger's FINISH entry, which is keyed by attempt id and carries no design field.

run_commit_chain.what_it_shows: run.py refuses a blind run while the ledger has uncommitted entries, and the lead commits the ledger after every attempt. Each run's git_head is therefore the commit that recorded the PREVIOUS run's ledger entry. The first run sits on the freeze commit itself and HEAD now names the last. The chain is unbroken with no gap and no extra link, which is independent evidence that the 11 attempts happened once each, in this order, under this freeze.

helper_scripts.location: scratchpad (robustness_*.py); NOT under out/s3/blind/analysis/, to avoid the filename collision described in note_filename_collision

note_filename_collision: out/s3/blind/analysis/ is written by several concurrent analyst sessions. This lens originally used build.py / pool.py / finish.py / md.py there; pool.py was overwritten by another lens's file of the same name (it reads _rows.json and writes pooled.json/pooled.md). No output of this lens was corrupted -- robustness.json was rebuilt end to end afterwards and every figure in it was re-derived from the raw run records -- but the collision is real and generic script names in that shared directory can silently clobber another session's work.

permutation_contribution.statement: Across all 11 records, every headline metric had min == median == max over the 5 permutations and distinct_answers == 1: the permutation contributes ZERO uncertainty. Quoting min/median/max for a blind figure would print one number three times.

precision.binding_uncertainty: the number of truth registers a rate is over, not the permutation

max_binomial_se_blind_10.formula: worst-case binomial standard error 0.5/sqrt(n); an independence assumption the design clustering below does not satisfy, so this is a FLOOR on the error

max_binomial_se_puzzle.formula: worst-case binomial standard error 0.5/sqrt(n); an independence assumption the design clustering below does not satisfy, so this is a FLOOR on the error

small_support_cells_blind_10.rule: score.SMALL_SUPPORT = 3: a kind with fewer registers is flagged, because one miss swings recall by more than 1/3

synchronizer_unit_credit_caveat.what: score.py strict mode scores a synchronizer register of a declared CHAIN UNIT only through its chain units, and a unit match credits every member register the structure holds.
synchronizer_unit_credit_caveat.consequence: 16 of the blind set's 18 synchronizer registers sit behind 2 result structures on 2 designs; a synchronizer recall denominator of 18 is NOT 18 independent trials

recommended_reporting: State each blind figure once; say the 5 permutations agreed exactly, do not print a min/median/max range.
Pooled blind rates: at most 2 significant figures (94 structure-kind registers -> best-case SE 5.2 pp).
Per-kind blind rates: give the fraction with its own denominator (e.g. 'n of 59' for counter), never a bare percentage.
lfsr_crc on the blind set is ONE design's 9 registers: report it as that design's result, not a rate.
Do not report a rate for any of the 5 (design, kind) cells with 1-2 registers or the 21 with none.
Never pool the puzzle with the blind 10: frozen code on a KNOWN design is not an out-of-sample test.

protocol.leakage_arm_note: the blind and puzzle runs were launched as --blind --jobs 5 with no --leakage, so the file-order arm of S3_DESIGN section 2 was NOT run on any blind design or on the puzzle. It was run on TEMPO only (out/s3/eval/runs/tempo-20260923T053247Z-ef7fc630631b.json: verdict 'pass', file-order arm's canonical answer identical to all 5 permutations). The blind set therefore has no direct test that the loader's own id order carries no signal; it has the weaker (but here exact) permutation spread.

tempo_reference_record.canonical_order_ties: 79 cells and 79 nets still shared a colour after refinement and fell back to id order (recorded as a note, not a problem); every flop, latch, clock gate, black box and port net was individualized. The answer was identical anyway.
tempo_reference_record.note: run.py's module docstring records that a review of 2026-09-22 found the recognizer NOT permutation invariant on TEMPO. On the FROZEN code that is no longer observable: this record's 5 permutations and the file-order arm all produced one canonical answer.

protocol.scorer_provenance_gap: score.py's provenance block has two categories only, TEMPO and not-TEMPO, so it labels the puzzle 'not the development design' / in_sample false -- exactly as it labels a blind design. out/s3/contamination.json is the record that says otherwise ('frozen code, known design, puzzle-informed development', never blind) and lists what the puzzle report must state. A reader of the puzzle score record alone would not learn this; the report must supply it.

out_of_sample_estimate_quoted_by_every_r.what_it_is: the synthetic corpus holdout: the PRE-PUBLISHED out-of-sample estimate. It is synthetic and written by this project (its own caveats say so), so the 10 drawn third-party designs remain the first out-of-sample test on designs this project did not write.
